categories.title: Asset Integrity Management & Engineering
categories.overview: This category brings inspection, engineering, operating and maintenance information into one coordinated integrity-management process. Its purpose is not simply to generate more inspection data, but to determine which assets and degradation mechanisms matter most, what information is required, when intervention is justified and how continued operation can be supported responsibly. The work may be applied to a single critical item, an operating unit or a wider portfolio covering static equipment, piping, tanks, structures and reliability-critical machinery.
challenges: Inspection programmes that repeat historical coverage without reflecting current risk or active damage mechanisms.
Incomplete, inconsistent or disconnected design, inspection, corrosion, process and maintenance data.
Ageing assets, changing operating conditions, temporary repairs and deferred maintenance requiring defensible prioritisation.
The need to translate technical findings into practical actions, operating limits, repair priorities and inspection intervals.
categories.delivery: IAIS UAE may begin with an asset and data review, establish the governing design and operating basis, identify credible deterioration, assess consequence and condition, and then build an integrity plan proportionate to risk. RBI, FFS, corrosion management, remaining-life assessment, integrity operating windows, reliability information and failure investigation can be combined where the decision requires more than one discipline. Recommendations are issued with assumptions, limitations, data gaps and action ownership clearly identified.
categories.assets: Pressure vessels, process piping, pipelines, storage tanks, boilers, heat exchangers, structures, rotating-equipment systems and integrated industrial facilities.
categories.value: Clients receive a prioritised and auditable basis for allocating inspection and maintenance resources, managing anomalies, supporting shutdown decisions and planning repair, replacement or life extension. The category is particularly valuable where many isolated reports exist but a single, risk-informed asset position is required.
categories.deliverables: Asset hierarchy and criticality review; damage-mechanism register; risk ranking; inspection and monitoring plan; FFS or remaining-life assessment; corrosion-control actions; integrity operating limits; anomaly register; management dashboard; life-extension roadmap and technical recommendations..
categories.outcome: Clear, traceable technical information that supports safety, compliance, reliability, maintenance prioritisation and lifecycle value.
services: Integrity Data Review and Technical Reporting

categories.title: NDT & Advanced Inspection Services
categories.overview: This category provides conventional and advanced nondestructive examination for detecting, locating, sizing and monitoring discontinuities without unnecessarily damaging the component. IAIS UAE selects methods according to material, geometry, thickness, accessibility, surface condition, expected defect orientation and the technical decision required. Conventional techniques establish broad quality and condition information, while advanced ultrasonic, electromagnetic, radiographic and monitoring methods can provide improved coverage, imaging or screening for complex assets.
challenges: Selecting a technique that is genuinely capable of detecting the expected flaw type rather than applying a familiar method by default.
Complex geometry, restricted access, coatings, insulation, elevated temperature or operating constraints that reduce examination effectiveness.
Differentiating screening indications from confirmed reportable conditions and choosing suitable complementary methods.
Producing traceable data that can be repeated, compared and used by inspection, quality and engineering teams.
categories.delivery: The service normally includes review of drawings and acceptance requirements, technique selection, procedure or scan-plan preparation, reference or calibration setup, controlled data acquisition, quality verification and evaluation by appropriately qualified personnel. Where required, IAIS UAE may combine VT, UT, PAUT, TOFD, FMC/TFM, radiography, surface methods, PEC, guided waves, PMI, hardness, metallography, acoustic emission or leak testing to address different degradation mechanisms and coverage limitations.
categories.assets: Welds, plates, forgings, castings, pipes, vessels, tanks, structural members, pressure components, insulated equipment and fabricated assemblies.
categories.value: Clients receive examination results matched to the inspection objective, with clear coverage, sensitivity, limitations and acceptance status. The category supports fabrication quality, shutdown inspection, baseline surveys, in-service condition assessment, repair verification and targeted follow-up of suspected degradation.
categories.deliverables: Approved procedure or technique sheet; scan plan; calibration and equipment records; examination report; indication register; images, radiographs or electronic datasets; coverage and limitation statement; acceptance status and follow-up recommendations..
categories.outcome: Clear, traceable technical information that supports safety, compliance, reliability, maintenance prioritisation and lifecycle value.
services: Full Matrix Capture and Total Focusing Method (FMC/TFM)

categories.title: Tube, Heat Exchanger & Boiler Inspection
categories.overview: This category focuses on the condition of tubes, tube ends, tube sheets and associated pressure parts within heat exchangers, condensers, boilers, air coolers and similar heat-transfer equipment. Tube failures can create leakage, contamination, efficiency loss, unplanned shutdown or safety exposure; therefore, the programme must match the tube material, geometry and expected deterioration. Electromagnetic, ultrasonic and visual methods may be combined to distinguish local wall loss, pitting, cracking, erosion, fretting and other service-related damage.
challenges: Large tube populations requiring efficient screening without losing location traceability.
Different materials and damage morphologies requiring different examination technologies and calibration references.
Restricted access, deposits, cleanliness, bends, fins, support plates and tube geometry affecting signal quality.
Converting individual indications into defensible plugging, repair, replacement and remaining-condition recommendations.
categories.delivery: IAIS UAE may review equipment drawings, tube material and layout, service chemistry, failure history and previous data before developing the inspection strategy. ECT, RFET, NFT, IRIS, MFL, PSEC and complementary methods are selected according to capability and limitation. Data are acquired using controlled channel identification and evaluated to establish distribution, severity and repeatability. Suspect results may be verified using an alternative technique or additional preparation.
categories.assets: Shell-and-tube heat exchangers, condensers, boilers, economisers, superheaters, reheaters, evaporators, air coolers and fin-fan tube systems.
categories.value: The client gains a tube-by-tube condition picture that supports safe return to service, plugging limits, maintenance planning, bundle replacement strategy and inspection interval review. Trend comparison can identify whether degradation is isolated, process-related or developing across defined zones.
categories.deliverables: Tube identification and layout validation; technique and calibration records; tube condition map; indication classification; severity distribution; plug/repair recommendations; comparison with historical data; equipment-level condition summary and next-inspection advice..
categories.outcome: Clear, traceable technical information that supports safety, compliance, reliability, maintenance prioritisation and lifecycle value.
services: Tube Condition Assessment and Remaining-Life Evaluation

categories.title: Storage Tank Integrity
categories.overview: This category provides lifecycle integrity support for aboveground and other industrial storage tanks from fabrication and commissioning through in-service inspection, shutdown examination, repair and return to service. Tank integrity depends on the combined condition of the floor, shell, roof, nozzles, appurtenances, foundations, settlement behaviour, coatings, linings and secondary containment. IAIS UAE develops the scope around stored product, tank design, corrosion history, operating constraints and the governing inspection framework.
challenges: Hidden floor corrosion and localised product-side or soil-side degradation that may threaten containment.
Settlement, distortion, out-of-roundness, roof deterioration and foundation conditions affecting structural behaviour.
Balancing in-service screening with the more extensive access available during an out-of-service inspection.
Integrating large quantities of MFL, ultrasonic, visual, dimensional and repair information into one defensible tank assessment.
categories.delivery: The programme may include API 653 or EEMUA-based planning, visual inspection, floor MFL screening, ultrasonic confirmation and mapping, shell thickness measurement, roof and structural inspection, settlement/verticality/roundness survey, robotic inspection, vacuum-box testing and repair surveillance. Findings are correlated with construction details, previous repairs, corrosion trends and minimum required thickness or remaining-life calculations where authorised.
categories.assets: Fixed-roof and floating-roof tanks, terminal tanks, refinery tanks, water and chemical tanks, tank foundations, bunds, associated appurtenances and pressurised storage interfaces.
categories.value: Clients receive a clear view of containment risk, repair urgency, inspection coverage and the basis for continued service or shutdown work. The integrated category reduces fragmentation between floor, shell, roof, geometry and repair records and supports more efficient planning of maintenance windows.
categories.deliverables: Tank inspection report; component condition register; floor and shell maps; MFL/UT data; settlement and dimensional survey; leak-test records; repair and alteration inspection records; corrosion rate; remaining life; next-inspection recommendation and return-to-service dossier..
categories.outcome: Clear, traceable technical information that supports safety, compliance, reliability, maintenance prioritisation and lifecycle value.

categories.title: Pressure Equipment & Static Asset Integrity
categories.overview: This category addresses the integrity of pressure vessels, boilers, columns, reactors, exchangers, drums, separators, heaters, air coolers and associated pressure-retaining systems. These assets may be exposed to internal corrosion, erosion, cracking, creep, fatigue, embrittlement, thermal damage, CUI and process-specific deterioration. Effective inspection must connect the equipment design and materials to the actual service environment and provide sufficient evidence for maintenance, repair or continued-operation decisions.
challenges: Complex damage mechanisms occurring at welds, nozzles, attachments, internals, linings and temperature-transition zones.
Limited internal access or the need to assess equipment without opening it.
Uncertain or localised thinning and flaws requiring remaining-life or fitness-for-service evaluation.
Coordinating inspection, repair, pressure-system requirements and shutdown schedules across multiple disciplines.
categories.delivery: IAIS UAE may prepare API 510 or asset-specific inspection plans, complete internal and external examination, thickness surveys, targeted NDT, CUI assessment, exchanger or boiler inspection, flange/valve/PRD support, NII planning and repair surveillance. Inspection findings are evaluated against the applicable equipment basis and may be transferred into authorised FFS, remaining-life or repair-engineering scopes when acceptance cannot be established directly.
categories.assets: Pressure vessels, columns, reactors, drums, separators, boilers, fired heaters, heat exchangers, air coolers, valves, flanged joints and relief-device interfaces.
categories.value: The client receives a coherent equipment condition position rather than separate technique reports. This supports safe operation, shutdown prioritisation, repair definition, anomaly management, interval review and longer-term replacement or life-extension planning.
categories.deliverables: Equipment inspection plan; internal/external examination records; thickness grids and corrosion trends; NDT reports; anomaly register; CUI findings; repair/alteration surveillance; NII assessment; remaining-life/FFS inputs and next-inspection recommendations..
categories.outcome: Clear, traceable technical information that supports safety, compliance, reliability, maintenance prioritisation and lifecycle value.

categories.title: Piping & Pipeline Integrity
categories.overview: This category provides integrity support for process piping, utility systems, plant pipelines and transmission lines throughout construction, operation, maintenance and repair. Piping systems contain many branches, fittings, dead legs, injection points, supports, insulated sections and welded joints where service conditions can concentrate degradation. IAIS UAE organises the scope by corrosion circuit, damage mechanism and line criticality so that inspection locations are technically justified and repeatable.
challenges: Extensive line populations with limited inspection resources and incomplete circuit or thickness-history data.
Localised corrosion, erosion, CUI, vibration fatigue, cracking and mechanical damage concentrated at specific features.
Screening long or inaccessible sections while recognising the limitations of indirect techniques.
Translating wall-thickness and weld data into remaining strength, repair priorities and future inspection intervals.
categories.delivery: The programme may include API 570 planning, circuitisation, pipeline condition review, thickness measurement, corrosion mapping, guided-wave screening, CUI assessment, focused dead-leg and injection-point inspection, small-bore and branch examination, support surveys, weld inspection and flange/bolting assessment. Results are compared with design requirements and historical data to establish corrosion rates, minimum remaining thickness and action priorities.
categories.assets: Process and utility piping, cross-country pipelines, station piping, transfer lines, manifolds, branches, dead legs, injection points, insulated circuits, supports, flanges and welded joints.
categories.value: Clients obtain a location-controlled basis for managing loss-of-containment risk, selecting repairs, prioritising insulation removal and setting appropriate monitoring or inspection intervals. The approach also improves the quality of isometrics, circuit registers and historical data for future integrity programmes.
categories.deliverables: Piping/pipeline register; corrosion circuits; inspection plan; marked-up isometrics; thickness and corrosion maps; guided-wave or weld reports; CUI and support findings; corrosion rates; remaining-strength inputs; repair recommendations and interval assessment..
categories.outcome: Clear, traceable technical information that supports safety, compliance, reliability, maintenance prioritisation and lifecycle value.

categories.title: Marine, Offshore & Structural Integrity
categories.overview: This category supports ships, offshore units, platforms, ports and industrial structures exposed to seawater, dynamic loading, fatigue, impact, coating breakdown and difficult access. Marine and offshore assets require condition evidence that is location-controlled, compatible with owner and classification requirements and suitable for repair or docking decisions. Structural inspection also demands attention to load paths, connections, nodes, weld details, corrosion traps and previous modifications.
challenges: Widespread corrosion and pitting across large structures where repeatable location identification is essential.
Fatigue-sensitive welds, splash-zone degradation, coating failure and restricted-access compartments.
Coordinating rope access, confined spaces, marine operations, survey attendance and repair windows.
Separating inspection evidence from the formal acceptance or approval responsibilities of class, flag or statutory authorities.
categories.delivery: IAIS UAE may provide marine UTM, hull and tank gauging, structural and weld inspection, offshore platform or rig surveys, FPSO/FSO support, lifting-equipment and crane inspection, coating surveys, splash-zone support, rope-access inspection and pre-docking preparation. Work is planned against structural drawings, survey locations, previous thickness data and the applicable owner/class requirements, with competent access and inspection personnel.
categories.assets: Ships, hulls, decks, bulkheads, ballast and cargo tanks, offshore platforms, jack-up rigs, FPSO/FSO units, jetties, cranes, lifting structures and marine-access systems.
categories.value: The client receives reliable survey evidence for maintenance, steel renewal, coating work, docking preparation, repair planning and attending-surveyor review. Combining access, measurement and structural condition information can reduce repeated mobilisation and improve coverage during limited maintenance windows.
categories.deliverables: Survey plan; location and compartment register; UTM data; structural and weld findings; coating condition report; annotated drawings and photographs; repair/steel-renewal list; load-test support records; pre-docking dossier and class-survey support package..
categories.outcome: Clear, traceable technical information that supports safety, compliance, reliability, maintenance prioritisation and lifecycle value.

categories.title: Remote Access, Robotics & Digital Inspection
categories.overview: This category uses rope access, confined-space systems, drones, robotic platforms, remote visual tools, thermal imaging and digital survey technologies to obtain inspection information from difficult, hazardous, elevated, enclosed or extensive areas. The purpose is to improve safe access and data coverage while reducing scaffolding, shutdown time or personnel exposure where practicable. The technology is selected according to the inspection objective; access innovation does not replace the need for a technically capable sensor and a controlled examination process.
challenges: Reaching elevated, enclosed, hot, contaminated, geometrically complex or operationally restricted locations.
Maintaining stable sensor position, coverage traceability, image quality and scale when inspection is performed remotely.
Managing aviation, confined-space, rope-access, offshore and site-specific permissions and safety controls.
Converting large image, thermal, point-cloud or robotic datasets into concise and actionable defect information.
categories.delivery: IAIS UAE may combine specialised access planning with drone visual/thermal surveys, robotic crawling, RVI, borescope/videoscope work, stack and flare inspection, elevated-structure surveys, digital defect mapping, photogrammetry, 3D mapping, laser scanning and thermal imaging. Each programme defines coverage, resolution, reference scale, environmental limits, data quality checks and the locations that require close-up or complementary NDT confirmation.
categories.assets: Flare stacks, chimneys, tanks, pipe racks, roofs, façades, offshore structures, confined vessels, internal cavities, pipelines, elevated steelwork and large industrial sites.
categories.value: Clients can obtain earlier condition visibility, reduce conventional-access dependency and preserve a repeatable digital record for engineering, maintenance and progress comparison. The strongest value is achieved when remote data are integrated with asset drawings, inspection history and targeted close-up confirmation.
categories.deliverables: Access and flight/mission plan; coverage map; high-resolution imagery; thermal survey; robotic or RVI record; defect map; annotated photographs; photogrammetric model; point cloud or dimensional survey; limitation statement and follow-up inspection priorities..
categories.outcome: Clear, traceable technical information that supports safety, compliance, reliability, maintenance prioritisation and lifecycle value.

categories.title: PWHT, Heat Treatment & Thermal Services
categories.overview: This category provides controlled heating, soaking and cooling of welds, components and refractory systems to meet specified metallurgical, fabrication or process requirements. Successful heat treatment depends on more than reaching a target temperature: heating rates, temperature gradients, soak duration, thermocouple placement, insulation, power distribution and cooling must be controlled and documented. IAIS UAE develops the arrangement from the material, thickness, geometry, welding procedure and applicable thermal cycle.
challenges: Uneven geometry and heat losses producing unacceptable gradients or incomplete heated-band control.
Incorrect thermocouple number, placement or attachment affecting the reliability of recorded temperatures.
Power, cable, insulation and equipment-capacity limitations at field locations.
Demonstrating that the complete cycle complied with the approved procedure and resolving interruptions or deviations.
categories.delivery: The service may include local or furnace PWHT, resistance or induction heating, preheat/post-heat, stress relieving, controlled heating/cooling, refractory dry-out, thermal-cycle monitoring, thermocouple installation, chart recording, hardness verification, procedure preparation, equipment rental and technical manpower. Heating zones, control zones and monitoring points are planned before mobilisation, and the cycle is supervised with calibrated equipment and traceable records.
categories.assets: Piping welds, pressure vessels, pipelines, heavy-wall components, structural welds, castings, fabricated assemblies, furnaces, boilers and refractory-lined equipment.
categories.value: Clients receive a controlled and auditable thermal process that supports weld quality, dimensional stability, hydrogen control, residual-stress reduction and code compliance. Clear planning reduces the risk of cycle rejection, rework, schedule disruption and disputes over temperature records.
categories.deliverables: Heat-treatment procedure; equipment and power plan; heating/insulation layout; thermocouple map; calibration records; time-temperature charts; cycle compliance report; deviation record; hardness results and equipment/manpower mobilisation documentation..
categories.outcome: Clear, traceable technical information that supports safety, compliance, reliability, maintenance prioritisation and lifecycle value.

categories.title: Materials, Corrosion & Failure Analysis
categories.overview: This category investigates what a material is, how it has changed in service, why it has deteriorated or failed and what action can prevent recurrence. Field verification, metallography, chemical analysis, mechanical testing, corrosion evaluation, coating inspection and cathodic-protection assessment provide complementary evidence. The programme is built around a defined technical question and preserves traceability from sampling or field location through testing, interpretation and recommendation.
challenges: Distinguishing the primary failure mechanism from secondary damage created after the initiating event.
Obtaining representative samples or field observations without destroying essential evidence.
Reconciling material certificates, PMI results, microstructure, mechanical properties, service conditions and fracture features.
Converting laboratory or field findings into practical repair, material-selection, monitoring and operating recommendations.
categories.delivery: IAIS UAE may perform or coordinate material verification, PMI, in-situ replication, microstructure review, chemical and mechanical testing, hardness, tensile, impact and bend testing, corrosion evaluation, coating surveys, cathodic-protection assessment and welding qualification support. Failure investigations follow an evidence plan covering background, visual examination, NDT, sampling, laboratory work, causal evaluation and review of credible alternative explanations.
categories.assets: Failed or degraded piping, vessels, welds, fasteners, castings, forgings, structures, coatings, cathodically protected systems, fabricated components and qualification specimens.
categories.value: Clients receive evidence-based conclusions that can support immediate containment, repair selection, material substitution, operating changes and prevention of repeat failures. The category also improves procurement and fabrication decisions by verifying material properties and welding-performance requirements before service.
categories.deliverables: Evidence and sample register; PMI/chemistry report; micrographs and metallurgical interpretation; mechanical-test results; corrosion/coating/CP assessment; failure mechanism; root-cause analysis; material or welding qualification records and corrective/preventive recommendations..
categories.outcome: Clear, traceable technical information that supports safety, compliance, reliability, maintenance prioritisation and lifecycle value.

categories.title: Quality, Vendor & Project Inspection
categories.overview: This category provides independent surveillance and verification throughout procurement, fabrication, installation, testing, commissioning and handover. The objective is to confirm that materials, workmanship, processes, tests and documentation comply with approved purchase, code and project requirements before equipment or work progresses beyond critical stages. IAIS UAE can support individual source visits or provide continuous quality surveillance across vendors, sites and project packages.
challenges: Complex purchase specifications and inspection plans with unclear hold, witness, review and surveillance responsibilities.
Material, welding, testing or documentation nonconformities discovered too late for efficient correction.
Schedule risk caused by delayed submittals, incomplete records, unresolved punch items or poor manufacturing visibility.
Maintaining independence, traceability and consistent reporting across multiple vendors, locations and disciplines.
categories.delivery: IAIS UAE may review ITPs and procedures, verify incoming materials and traceability, witness fabrication, welding, NDT, dimensional checks, heat treatment and pressure tests, perform vendor/source inspection, monitor progress, complete pre-shipment inspection and support installation, commissioning and handover. Observations and nonconformities are documented against specific requirements and tracked to an agreed disposition or closure status.
categories.assets: Pressure equipment, piping, valves, fabricated structures, skids, tanks, machinery packages, castings, forgings, project materials, site installations and multidisciplinary handover systems.
categories.value: Clients gain earlier visibility of conformity and progress, reducing the probability of rejected equipment, site rework, documentation gaps and delayed commissioning. Independent records also strengthen release decisions, supplier performance review and final project acceptance.
categories.deliverables: ITP and document review; visit and surveillance reports; material/welding/test verification; nonconformity and punch list; progress/expediting status; release note; pre-shipment report; commissioning records; handover dossier review and completion verification..
categories.outcome: Clear, traceable technical information that supports safety, compliance, reliability, maintenance prioritisation and lifecycle value.

categories.title: Technical Manpower & Specialist Deployment
categories.overview: This category supplies inspection, integrity, materials, welding, quality and PWHT specialists for defined technical assignments. Deployment may support a short inspection campaign, shutdown, emergency response, vendor assignment, construction project or long-term site requirement. The emphasis is on matching verified competence and relevant experience to the actual duty, not simply providing headcount. Roles, reporting lines, deliverables and technical authority are established before mobilisation.
challenges: Matching certifications alone without confirming sector experience, equipment familiarity or the competence required for the specific task.
Rapid mobilisation across visa, medical, offshore, access, security and client onboarding requirements.
Maintaining consistent technical supervision, reporting and quality across multiple personnel, shifts or sites.
Separating manpower provision from engineering approval and ensuring responsibilities are clear between IAIS UAE, the deployed personnel and the client.
categories.delivery: IAIS UAE may deploy integrity/RBI/FFS engineers, API inspectors, NDT Level II/III personnel, advanced NDT and tube specialists, welding/QAQC inspectors, mechanical/piping inspectors, corrosion/coating inspectors, rope-access personnel, PWHT technicians, metallurgists, coordinators, supervisors and integrated shutdown teams. Candidate review can include certification, experience, interview, competency checks and client approval before mobilisation, followed by attendance and performance monitoring.
categories.assets: Shutdowns, turnarounds, construction projects, fabrication yards, operating plants, terminals, marine/offshore assignments, vendor locations and long-term integrity programmes.
categories.value: Clients can scale specialised technical resources to project demand without compromising role clarity or reporting control. Group-backed mobilisation may provide access to wider inspection and engineering experience, while the actual UAE assignment remains subject to licence, visa, competency and client requirements.
categories.deliverables: Resource plan; role and responsibility matrix; CV/certification dossier; competency and client-approval status; mobilisation schedule; attendance/timesheets; daily or periodic reports; technical supervision records; replacement/continuity plan and assignment close-out..
categories.outcome: Clear, traceable technical information that supports safety, compliance, reliability, maintenance prioritisation and lifecycle value.
